expertNote.title: Apple's EU app-distribution terms preserve platform control
expertNote.summary: The comment argues that alternative iOS distribution still requires an Apple relationship, while distinguishing user-paid OS APIs from developer tooling such as Xcode and the SDK.

evidenceSpans.text: The main issue that the DMA was about still remains: Apple retains ultimate control over app developers' dealings with users.
The OS APIs that most apps use are already paid-for by the user when they buy the device.
Xcode and the SDK overall aren't paid for by users

expertNote.title: The printer solution bridges an existing driver
expertNote.summary: Claude did not write a native macOS printer driver; the solution used HP's proprietary Linux driver in a VM and bridged it to macOS, with a root launcher that weakens security.

evidenceSpans.text: Claude didn't write a driver. It basically used HP's existing proprietary driver in a Linux VM on macOS, and just bridged that to macOS.
It also requires a root launcher that runs code from the user ~/.hp1008 dir, so security is weakened.

expertNote.title: Claude-assisted reverse engineering produced a portable controller tool
expertNote.summary: The author used Claude with ILSpy and Wireshark to reverse engineer a USB golf-cart controller, producing a portable C library and CLI that worked in practice.

evidenceSpans.text: Claude walked me through using ILSpy on the .NET assembly, using Wireshark to capture the protocol over USB, and to completely map out all of the functionality in the Windows application.
The output was a portable C library and CLI program which, so far, has worked well.

expertNote.title: Emergency-alert filtering can hide critical warnings
expertNote.summary: In South Korea, frequent low-severity emergency notifications can be filtered, but the same filter may suppress a critical artillery warning.

evidenceSpans.text: If you're in South Korea, you can expect to get around half a dozen emergency notifications every day.
You can set your phone to filter these out, but then you'll also miss the notification about North Korea commencing artillery bombardment.

expertNote.title: GrapheneOS retains Android app compatibility that Linux phones lack
expertNote.summary: GrapheneOS can run existing Android applications, including banking apps that commonly refuse to support Linux phones.

evidenceSpans.text: All the existing apps are on Android and iOS. Graphene lets you run them.
You can't have a bank account on a Linux phone* because they won't let you, but you can on Android including on Graphene.

expertNote.title: Squashed tarballs and delayed forms may not satisfy GPL source form
expertNote.summary: GrapheneOS argues that discarding commit metadata into a tarball and requiring a delayed manual form do not meet GPLv2's preferred-form and customary-interchange language.

evidenceSpans.text: throwing away the metadata of however many commits and squashing them into a messy tarball is not the "preferred form of the work for making modifications"
a manual process where you have to fill out a form in order to get a Google Drive link a week later is not "a medium customarily used for software interchange"

expertNote.title: AOSP publishing changes caused release and device-strategy costs
expertNote.summary: A GrapheneOS maintainer reports missing Pixel tags and releases, weeks of port delay, slower source-request handling, a Motorola partnership, and continued Pixel use for security rather than supportability.

evidenceSpans.text: Google has stopped pushing Git tags for some Android source code
They stopped pushing tags for any of the Pixel kernel or userspace driver repositories to AOSP.
These changes directly led to our Motorola partnership.
Recently, they've been taking weeks or longer to get back to us for the requests
For us, Pixels are being used due to security rather than ease of supporting them.

expertNote.title: Mental day-of-week calculation using memorable key dates

a 9-to-5 job at 7-11

if I’d recently opened the AliExpress iOS app (ie. it was backgrounded) my car audio would freak out thinking I was giving it an audio command.
Killing the AliExpress app immediately fixed the problem.

expertNote.title: Package registries obscured the Arrayref incident state
expertNote.summary: The removed GitHub repository and crates.io package version lacked clear incident, yank, or advisory state, leading the commenter to conclude crates.io was unprepared for the response.

GitHub really needs something finer-grain then just pretending the repo never existed during these incidents.

does this also allow websites to continue running in the background on mobile browsers?

expertNote.title: Agent communication preferences degrade over long sessions

The baked in communication style of these models is so obnoxious it's impacting my work.

expertNote.title: Reduced fMRI activity does not establish harm
expertNote.summary: dlPFC deactivation occurs in many immersive tasks; lower activity during one task only identifies involvement patterns and does not by itself show a good or bad effect.

evidenceSpans.text: dlPFC deactivation is observed in a lot of immersive tasks.
Having them be less active during a task doesn't imply that it's good or bad. It just shows you which parts of the brain are involved in that task.
It would have been more interesting if they compared to something, like watching a long involved movie or playing video games, but they didn't.

expertNote.title: Aggressive client retry behavior amplified an outage
expertNote.summary: A latent VS Code retry loop increased Copilot Token Service traffic roughly tenfold; the commenter argues retry backoff should be explicitly tested rather than treated as an incidental bug.

evidenceSpans.text: Delayed replies to a single internal endpoint triggered a latent retry bug in VS Code that amplified traffic by approximately 10x and caused delayed recovery for the Copilot Token Service.
client retry doesn't have a unit test which ensures the retry back off behaviour is functioning exactly as designed

expertNote.title: Agent-generated microservices move rather than remove complexity
expertNote.summary: Agents reasoning over isolated code may miss product-wide interactions, so multiplying microservices can create a rapidly moving architecture whose complexity exceeds available context.

evidenceSpans.text: Agents aren't very good at carrying the entire model in their context, so when they reason about a small piece of code, they often come up with something that hurts other parts of the code
The complexity hasn't been replaced, only moved.

expertNote.title: Overload should cause graceful degradation, not collapse
expertNote.summary: Capacity is finite; overloaded systems should shed low-priority traffic, avoid retrying rejected requests, trigger client throttling, and isolate abusive clients.

evidenceSpans.text: this complex system collapses (rather than degrade gracefully) when demand exceeds capacity
When components reach capacity limits, the excess traffic of the lowest priority should be rejected.
Rejected traffic should not be retried
Traffic isolation should be applied

expertNote.title: The head-unit malware arrives through first-party OTA updates
expertNote.summary: The malware affects cheap aftermarket Android head units through official OTA updates; it does not self-propagate to all Android head units or affect Android Auto, whose software primarily runs on the phone.

evidenceSpans.text: the malware in question is delivered through official first-party OTA updates on cheap Chinese aftermarket head units that happen to run Android.

It cannot self-propagate to any Android-based head unit, nor does it affect Android Auto which is a "dumb" screen mirroring protocol with the bulk of the software running on the connected phone rather than the head unit.
cheap generic Android TV streaming boxes, which often come pre-infected from the factory with residential proxies and other malware
